summary: APM feed s128_double is degraded: 100% of traffic is untagged (required VLANs 10, 20 missing) and microbursts peak at 27.22 Gbps on a 10 Gbps tool port (272% overload), causing segmentation blindness and burst drops.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or TAP aggregation is stripping 802.1Q tags before delivery. 100% of packets are untagged despite APM requiring VLANs 10 and 20, indicating broker port configured to strip tags, VLAN translation/removal policy, or SPAN from access ports instead of trunk/TAP preserving tags.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM cannot segment or correlate performance by VLAN/application tier (10, 20). Transactions appear as single flat network, breaking per-VLAN SLAs, filtering, and tenant isolation visibility.

recommended_fix.why: Re-enable 802.1Q preservation on broker egress and ensure ingress is from trunk/TAP that forwards VLANs 10,20 so APM receives correctly tagged traffic for segmentation.

findings.root_cause: Aggregate feed is bursting to 27.22 Gbps in 1ms intervals into a single 10 Gbps APM port without load balancing or shaping. Multiple high-rate inputs are aggregated directly to one tool port, exceeding line rate by 172%.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will drop packets during bursts due to port buffer overrun, causing incomplete transaction records, inaccurate latency/error calculations, and missed performance anomalies despite needing both directions.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across 3x10G APM ports (or APM cluster) with flow-aware hashing to keep bursts under 80% per port and preserve both directions per flow for APM correlation.
